overview.overview:
Minnesota is expected to favor the Democratic presidential nominee, with an expected lead of about 10.5 points and a plausible range from a narrow one-point edge to a 20-point win. The state voted Democratic by 7.1 points in 2020 and by 4.2 points in 2024, so its recent results point to a consistent but narrower advantage. Minnesota has also leaned more Democratic than the nation as a whole, and the broader national environment currently tilts toward Democrats.

No public 2028 polls for Minnesota are available, so the outlook rests on past results and the 2026 statewide picture, where Democratic-leaning margins of about 10 points in the Senate race and about 13 points in the governor's race are projected. The listed home-state candidate is Republican Royce White. Minnesota is unlikely to decide the Electoral College.
overview.watch: The arrival of Minnesota-specific 2028 polling, or a further narrowing of the state's margin relative to the nation, could shift how competitive the contest appears.
key_factors: Minnesota's Democratic lean has held in the last two presidential elections, though the margin narrowed from 2020 to 2024.
The state has leaned more Democratic than the nation, and the national environment favors Democrats.
Projected 2026 statewide margins for Senate and governor are Democratic-leaning and wider than the 2024 presidential result.
